# Ādittajātaka (Ja 424)

**ID:** Ja 424
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Ādittajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** When Your House is Burning Down
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja424
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ādittajātaka* (Ja 424) is a canonical Jātaka tale belonging to the Aṭṭhakanipāta [Fausböll 1883; Fausböll 1897]. In later editorial and commentary references, it is also cited as the *Sovīrajātaka*—drawn from its narrative opening (*atīte Sovīraraṭṭhe*)—which was corrupted in certain manuscripts into the ghost title *Sucirajātaka* [Fausböll 1897]. The canonical verses open with the fire metaphor *ādittasmiṃ* ("when [a house] is burning down") [Fausböll 1883; SuttaCentral]. According to the nidāna, the Buddha recounted this tale while residing at Jetavana concerning the "incomparable gift" (*asadisadāna*) offered by the King of Kosala, who had carefully investigated and selected the supreme field of merit headed by the Buddha before bestowing his offering [Fausböll 1883; SuttaCentral]. Illustrating that the wise of old also gave gifts after examination (*viceyyadāna*), the Master recounted his past life as King Bharata in the Sovīra realm alongside Queen Samuddavijayā (identified as Rāhula's mother), who supported Paccekabuddhas and practiced lifelong liberality [Fausböll 1883].

Scholars have noted the narrative's emphasis on discriminatory giving, wherein the king provides for ascetics, brāhmaṇas, and the poor or wretched (*kapaṇa*), while conveying that gifts offered to spiritually accomplished mendicants produce superior merit compared to charity directed merely toward the ordinary poor [Fenn 1994].

SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels to the text's verses in SN 1.33 (*Sādhusutta*), SN 1.41 (*Ādittasutta*), and AN 3.52 (*Dutiyadvebrāhmaṇasutta*), with a thematic connection to the *Aṅkurapetavatthu* (Pv 21) [SuttaCentral]. This is corroborated by DharmaNexus and early translators, who identify substantial verse reuse between this Jātaka and the *Devatā Saṁyutta* (SN 1), specifically an alignment between §0.4–2.4 of the Jātaka and SN 1.41 (§41.1.4–41.3.4) at a 0.95 similarity score [DharmaNexus; Mrs. Rhys Davids 1917]. DharmaNexus also records verse matches in the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* and cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Patna Dharmapada* and the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (D0326) [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels (SuttaCentral): SN 1.33 Sādhusutta; SN 1.41 Ādittasutta; AN 3.52 Dutiyadvebrāhmaṇasutta
- Mentioned in (SuttaCentral): Pv 21 Aṅkurapetavatthu
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Devatā Saṁyutta (SN 1) (§0.4–2.4 ↔ §41.1.4–41.3.4); Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§3.1–8.4 ↔ §4176_3–4194); Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0502a) (§4.4–5.4 ↔ §2834–2837)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): Patna Dharmapada (SA_K14_dhppat_u) [sa]; ཆེད་དུ་བརྗོད་པའི་ཚོམས། (udānavarga) (D0326) [bo]; BO_K10_Dx_H0290 [bo]

**Sources**

- [SuttaCentral] SuttaCentral record for ja424 — Provides English title, blurb on the story of the present and incomparable gift, and parallel citations (SN 1.33, SN 1.41, AN 3.52, Pv 21).
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus text-reuse database — Identifies internal verse reuse with SN 1, Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā, and Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā, as well as cross-language alignments with the Patna Dharmapada and Udānavarga.
- [Mrs. Rhys Davids 1917] Mrs. Rhys Davids, The Book of the Kindred Sayings, Vol. I (1917) — Notes the occurrence of the shared verses in the Āditta-Jātaka.
- [Fenn 1994] Mavis Lillian Fenn, Concept of Poverty in the Pali Canon (1994) — Analyzes the text's portrayal of gifts to religious mendicants versus the poor (kapaṇa).
- [Fausböll 1883] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka together with its Commentary, Vol. 3 (1883) — Provides the Pali text, incipit (ādittasmiṃ), nidāna, and character identifications (Bharatarājā, Samuddavijayā).
- [Fausböll 1897] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka together with its Commentary, Vol. 7 (Index) (1897) — Explains the alternate title Sovīrajātaka and the manuscript scribal error Sucirajātaka.
